text:
maya: ran the kernel-candidate CI feeder last night against the ampere-v2 pool. overall pass rate looked fine but hit a sharp regression at seq_len=512 for the sm75 matmul kernel set.
liam: ugh, is that the kernel pick that favours tensor cores for 32/64 heads?
maya: yeah, autotuner picked fast_fused_v2 for most shapes but falls back to fallback_gemm on some hidden sizes. the perf delta: ~2.8x slower on tail cases.
cory: can you paste the microbench logs? especially latency p50/p95 and the kernel name mapping.
maya: sure — snippet from the nightly CSV:
```
model,seq_len,kernel,median_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tps
gpt2,128,fast_fused_v2,4.2,6.1,230
gpt2,256,fast_fused_v2,7.8,10.4,120
gpt2,512,fallback_gemm,31.4,42.0,28
```
maya: note the sudden jump at 512 where it falls back.
perf-bot: autotune run id: atune-2026-03-16-23. Candidate kernels: [fast_fused_v2, tiled_khav, fallback_gemm]. All candidates validated for correctness. Regression flag set for gpt2@512.
jen: is KV cache playing a role? 512 warm tokens + kv-resize overhead could trigger a different execution path.
maya: good call — I re-ran with cache warm-off and saw the kernel chose fast_fused_v2 and perf was back to ~8.1ms median. so KV copy path interacts with shape selection.
liam: that's... annoying. so our kernel selection logic is looking only at seq_len and d_model, not whether KV is in CPU vs GPU or whether warm cache append happens.
cory: also check batching heuristics — continuous batching combines prefix + new tokens which changes matmul dims. autotuner should consider "effective_seq" = prefix + new.
maya: agree. action: 1) update harness to record kv_state (hot/cold/cpu-gpu) and batch composition for each microbench sample; 2) add a targeted CI job simulating warm-cache append with seq_len combos; 3) add a rule in kernel picker to prefer fast_fused_v2 when KV is already on-device.
ops-bot: created ticket PERF-824: "kernel-picker: include KV cache residency + batch composition in autotune features" assigned to @liam due 2026-03-23.
liam: I'll take PERF-824. I'll also add a small probe that runs short microbench for seq in [64,128,256,512,1024] with kv warm/cold toggles each night.
alex: we should be careful with nightly load — maybe run the heavier probes only on a subset of nodes (perf-dedicated-2). I'll patch the CI matrix.
jen: one more thing — please add a regression alert that triggers when p95 increases >30% at any seq threshold compared to baseline. last time we missed the 512 cliff because overall pass rate was fine.
maya: noted. I'll update the harness and push a change to the autoselect logic after liam's probe data lands.
liam: plan: implement telemetry keys -> kernel_decision_context = {seq_len, d_model, kv_residency, batch_prefix_len, hardware_cap}. then feed to autotune scoring.
cory: yeah and log the chosen kernel id in per-request trace so we can correlate production regressions. small PRs preferred.
maya: thanks all. I'll upload the full raw CSV + perf traces to S3 at s3://redwood-perf/nightly/atune-2026-03-16/ for folks who want to dig in. ping me if you need access. :thumbsup:
